Exactly the degradation the commit message and receipt claim.
3_measuredFinding.whyActual0: The activated candidate branch carries no events of its own, so its branch revision reads 0, while the journal STREAM head is still 2 (the test asserts streamHeadRevision() === 2). The mirror asked the activated branch a question derived from the post-supersede store sequence (1), and got a quiet conflict instead of a refusal.
3_measuredFinding.riskStatementCorrect: YES. The append is aimed at expectedBranchId = the activated candidate with expectedRevision = nextMatchSequence. Nothing about branch identity is checked pre-guard. If the store's post-supersede next sequence had equalled the candidate branch's current revision, the guard-free append would have SUCCEEDED and put live-path match events onto the activated (rewind) branch at a revision derived from a number that no longer describes that history. Reachable in shape: a rewind that discards the whole tail leaves the store next sequence at 0 against a freshly-activated candidate at revision 0; more generally a candidate that accrued k rebuild events can coincide with a cut at the same number. The fixture's cut-at-1 case simply did not land on the coincidence, which is why the pre-guard symptom was a conflict rather than a corruption - the receipt says this plainly and does not overclaim.

S5R1.accuracy: CORRECT on every clause. (i) The guard keys on the effective head's branch id - MatchStreamJournalMirror.ts:163-165, the same signal S4's recovery and the live admission consult use. (ii) The refusal is permanent for a rewound stream: activateCandidateBranch installs the candidate as the effective head and nothing ever restores 'main'/'root', so isLivePathBranchId stays false. (iii) It is visible rather than silent, because every non-'mirrored' kind reaches recordProcessShadowComparison (DurableMatchStore.ts:1017-1025) - the intended fail-closed shape at mode 'shadow'. (iv) The S7 consequence is real: once S7 seeds the mirror at creation, every rewound match pins the mismatch counter above zero and blocks a shadow-parity claim. The instruction that the S7 receipt should SAY so rather than be surprised is the right carry-forward.
